titulo: Oracle (ORCL) Stock in 2026: What Moves the Price
descricao: Oracle (ORCL) analysis: a multibillion-dollar AI cloud backlog, heavy data center investment, and the risks behind the 2026 rally.
corpo:
Oracle has been known for decades for its databases and enterprise software, but in 2026 the company has increasingly been trading as a central piece of artificial intelligence infrastructure. Multibillion-dollar cloud contracts sit, on the same balance sheet, alongside heavy data center spending and growing debt — a contrast that helps explain why the stock draws so much attention from investors and traders.

This piece gathers the main figures and factors cited about Oracle (ticker ORCL, listed on the NYSE) with data from June 2026, as publicly disclosed at the time. The figures change over time, and nothing here should be read as a recommendation to buy or sell — the goal is to map what was moving the stock at that moment, to help understand the kind of factor worth watching.

What Oracle does and where its revenue comes from

Oracle sells databases, enterprise applications, and cloud infrastructure to large organizations — governments, banks, healthcare networks, telecom operators, and Fortune 500 companies. Much of the revenue comes from long-term subscriptions, which gives the company a more predictable flow than the traditional model of one-off software licenses.

In recent years, the company's focus has shifted to cloud computing, especially the Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) platform, which offers processing power, storage, and networking — including services specifically aimed at training and running artificial intelligence models. In this market, Oracle competes with names like Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, but it leans on a specific advantage: a customer base that has already used its databases and applications for years and can gradually migrate those workloads to Oracle's own cloud.

The numbers on the radar in June 2026

According to Yahoo Finance data from June 2026, Oracle had a market value of $662.4 billion, with the stock trading at $230.33 and up 18.4% year to date at that point. The price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio stood at 41.4, dropping to 28.6 on the forward P/E — a gap signaling that the market was already pricing in significant profit growth for the following periods. The 52-week range went from $134.57 to $345.72, and the dividend paid represented a yield of 0.9% per year, with earnings per share (EPS) of $5.57.

The growth engine: AI cloud contracts

The main factor cited to explain interest in the stock was demand for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for artificial intelligence workloads. The company had signed large, long-term contracts with names like OpenAI, Meta, and xAI, which helped build a backlog of remaining performance obligations (RPO) estimated at $553 billion in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 — a jump of approximately 325% from the year before. That number works as an indicator of contracted revenue for the coming years, and any sign that it keeps growing, or that new AI and cloud contracts are being signed, tends to be closely watched by the market.

The other side of the coin: spending and negative cash flow

Building capacity to meet this volume of contracts requires heavy investment. Oracle had been spending tens of billions of dollars a year building new AI-focused data centers, which pushed the company's free cash flow to negative $394 million, even with a historically profitable software base. The company's annual revenue, approximately $57.4 billion, was growing 8.4% year over year — a solid pace, but much slower than the growth of the cloud contract backlog itself.

This is the central point of the debate around the stock: if the market gains confidence that this heavy investment will generate a proportional return in the coming years, the rally tends to hold up or even extend; if cash consumption stays high and doubts emerge about the ability to service the debt tied to this expansion, the stock tends to come under pressure.

Factors that called for ongoing attention

Among the points analysts used to monitor at the time, based on the available data, were: the quarterly evolution of the cloud contract backlog, the pace of data center capacity expansion relative to real demand, the level of revenue concentration among a few large AI customers, and the trajectory of the debt taken on to finance this expansion.

It's worth reinforcing that the numbers presented here reflect the situation disclosed in June 2026, the moment when the original piece was published, and may have changed significantly since then. This text is for educational purposes: it doesn't constitute a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold the stock, and any investment decision should take into account updated data, each investor's risk profile, and the fact that trading in the stock market always carries the possibility of capital loss.
